look_here_first: Start at the small annual taproot and opposite oval to elliptic leaves; then inspect the lower third of the 5-6 mm calyx tube for its distinctive swollen (saccate) side. Flowers have a 9-13 mm, noninflated pink corolla. Do not rely on color alone.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Accepted species and Texas state-level native occurrence; three target-zone county records have not been verified to project threshold.

morphology_keys.habit: Delicate annual, often 5-30 cm, slender taproot; dry rocky limestone habitat.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite, broadly elliptic or ovate, usually not over three times as long as wide, shortly petiolate, often slightly toothed and relatively glabrous; basal leaves sometimes purplish.
morphology_keys.flowers: Calyx about 5-6 mm, lower third of tube saccate; corolla pink 9-13 mm, not inflated.
best_field_traits: Annual root rather than persistent woody crown
Broadish opposite leaves on a slender plant
Saccate lower calyx tube; noninflated corolla

comparisons.key_distinctions: H. drummondii generally has narrower, often inrolled leaves, peppermint scent and calyx teeth converging over the opening at maturity; H. reverchonii is a persistent woody-based plant with usually larger stature and incompletely closing calyx teeth. H. serpyllifolia is accepted separately from the old H. reverchonii var. serpyllifolia name. Check mature calyx and basal crown before choosing a species.
comparisons.cautions: Hedeoma drummondii/reverchonii complex has difficult intermediates; color and scent are supporting, not stand-alone, evidence. Preserve uncertain IDs.

diagnostic_image_needs: Whole rooted annual showing taproot and habit
Side view of mature calyx showing saccate lower tube
Close-up corolla and calyx with millimeter scale
